And only the destruction of rural domestic industry can give the internal market of a country that extension and consistence which the capitalist mode of production requires.
summary: Destruction of rural domestic industry: expropriation creates both the industrial workforce and the domestic market for commodities.
explanation: When peasant households produced their own clothing and food, they had little need to buy manufactured commodities. Expropriating the peasantry destroyed domestic self-sufficiency, converting subsistence goods into commercial commodities and creating the domestic consumer market indispensable for large-scale capitalist industry.
context: Part VIII, Chapter 30: Reaction of the Agricultural Revolution on Industry
